selection_criteria: The 80 most recently published GitHub-reviewed advisories for the pip ecosystem as of 2026-08-07, capped at 2 per source repository and 1 per fixing commit, restricted to those carrying a CWE and a fixing-commit reference into their own repository whose parent is not a merge, whose fix diff is under 400 KB, and which touch reviewable Python source outside tests and docs. Ground-truth spans are the lines the fix removed, excluding spans that are entirely imports, version bumps or comments. Two fixing commits were then excluded by hand as bulk refactors whose spans mark remediation plumbing rather than the defect; the reasons are in benchmark/corpus/labelled-excluded.txt. NOT filtered by CWE: classes no 3a detector can emit are retained and reported as a stratum. Newest-first sampling makes the set post-cutoff for any model evaluated later.

findings.title: ReDoS reintroduced in magiclink URL regex

evidence.why: Replacing `[^_\W](?:[-\w]|\.(?!=$))*` with `[^_\W][-\w]*(?:\.[-\w.]+)*` introduces nested overlapping quantifiers (`[-\w]*` followed by repeated `[-\w.]+`), which can cause catastrophic backtracking on crafted input containing many dots/word chars, especially when this pattern fails to match against attacker-controlled text (e.g. markdown containing untrusted content).

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: ReDoS reintroduced by dropping negative lookahead in STAR_EM2

evidence.why: Changing `\*{2,}(?!\*)` to `\*{2,}` removes the lookahead that disambiguated star runs, reintroducing catastrophic backtracking potential in `((?:[^\*]|\*{2,})+?)` against strings with many asterisks, which are attacker-controlled markdown input.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: ReDoS reintroduced in SMART_UNDER_EM2 pattern

evidence.why: Same removal of `(?!_)` lookahead as UNDER_EM2, reintroducing ambiguous nested quantifier matching over underscore runs in untrusted markdown input.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: ReDoS reintroduced in SMART_STAR_EM2 pattern

evidence.why: Same removal of `(?!\*)` lookahead as STAR_EM2, reintroducing ambiguous nested quantifier matching over asterisk runs in untrusted markdown input.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: ReDoS reintroduced in SUP2 pattern

evidence.why: Removing `(?!\^)` lookahead from `\^{2,}(?!\^)` reintroduces catastrophic backtracking potential in `((?:[^\^\s]|\^{2,})+?)` against crafted caret sequences in markdown input.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: ReDoS reintroduced in SUB2 pattern

evidence.why: Removing `(?!~)` lookahead from `~{2,}(?!~)` reintroduces catastrophic backtracking potential in `((?:[^\s~]|~{2,})+?)` against crafted tilde sequences in markdown input.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

advisory.summary: LangGraph: Namespace prefix matching crosses segment boundaries in Postgres and SQLite stores

findings.title: Namespace prefix search no longer escapes LIKE metacharacters or enforces segment boundary

evidence.why: ns_condition is now a bare 'store.prefix LIKE %s' with pattern f"{_namespace_to_text(...)}%" and no ESCAPE clause or segment anchor, so a namespace label containing % or _ acts as a wildcard and a prefix like ('foo',) also matches ('foobar',), letting search cross into sibling namespaces it shouldn't reach.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: list_namespaces prefix/suffix match uses unescaped, unanchored LIKE

evidence.why: condition.match_type == 'prefix'/'suffix' now build 'prefix LIKE %s' with params like f"{_namespace_to_text(condition.path, handle_wildcards=True)}%" with no escaping of literal % or _ in path segments and no segment-boundary anchoring, so a caller-supplied namespace label with % or _ silently changes the query scope and can match unintended sibling namespaces.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: SQLite prefix search dropped case-sensitive/segment-boundary GLOB in favor of unescaped LIKE

evidence.why: prefix_filter_str now uses 's.prefix LIKE ?' with an unescaped, unanchored pattern instead of the previous exact/GLOB condition, so SQLite's case-insensitive, wildcard-sensitive LIKE both crosses namespace segment boundaries (foo matches foobar) and lets % or _ in a namespace label act as a wildcard, and also conflates differently-cased namespaces that get/put treat as distinct.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: list_namespaces prefix/suffix match on SQLite uses unescaped, unanchored LIKE

evidence.why: the new branch appends 'prefix LIKE ?' with f"{_namespace_to_text(cond.path, handle_wildcards=True)}%" (or leading %), removing the previous segment-aware regex/GLOB matching and escaping, so labels containing % or _ change match scope and prefixes are no longer anchored to segment boundaries.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

advisory.summary: LangGraph: Namespace prefix matching crosses segment boundaries in Postgres and SQLite stores

evidence.why: cb_on_headers_complete now returns 2 immediately whenever upgraded/CONNECT, causing llhttp to stop parsing without consuming the declared Content-Length/chunked body; this reverts the deferred-upgrade fix and means unread body bytes get treated as upgrade tail data even if the application declines the upgrade, enabling request smuggling.

findings.title: Removal of symlink-clamped path resolution enables archive escape

evidence.why: The diff removes _safe_resolve and replaces it with plain os.path.join(rootfs_dir, *rel_parts), so a malicious tar member can plant a symlink (e.g. evil -> /) earlier in the archive and a later entry named evil/passwd will be written through that symlink onto the host filesystem instead of being clamped inside rootfs_dir.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: Deferred hardlink copy no longer re-resolves endpoints, allowing symlink-redirected copy

evidence.why: for dest, src in deferred_links now uses paths computed once at member-processing time without re-resolving through _safe_resolve, so a symlink planted by a later archive member can redirect the hardlink copy's source or destination outside rootfs_dir, letting the archive read arbitrary host files via shutil.copy2.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: Symlink-derived hardlink source no longer clamped in rootfs

evidence.why: _defer_hardlink now builds link_src via os.path.join(rootfs_dir, *rel_lparts) directly instead of resolving through _safe_resolve, so a linkname routed through a previously planted symlink can cause shutil.copy2 to read a file from outside the intended rootfs subtree.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: Directory extraction no longer replaces pre-existing symlink

evidence.why: The removed 'if os.path.islink(dest): _remove_fstree(dest)' check means a directory member whose name collides with an earlier planted symlink will now have os.makedirs/chmod/utime operate through that symlink's target rather than replacing it, letting a crafted archive affect files outside the intended directory.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: Restore command drops _safe_dest symlink clamping for extraction and hardlink source

evidence.why: The diff removes the dest = _safe_dest(...) call before writes and the _safe_dest(..., follow_final=True) clamp on link_src, so a crafted backup archive containing a planted symlink can redirect both the write destination and the hardlink read source outside the container directory onto the host filesystem.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: _materialise_files drops _safe_resolve clamp, enabling symlink escape from build layers

evidence.why: host = os.path.join(rootfs_dir, arcname.lstrip('/')) replaces the previous _safe_resolve-based parent resolution, so an ADD'd tar or layer containing a symlink entry (e.g. evil -> /) followed by evil/passwd can cause files to be written outside rootfs_dir during image builds.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.
